b1-n-sinn: You spend hours on a job that nobody will ever use. Your friend asks what good it does and what goal it serves.
In class, the teacher reads a poem and asks what the lines are really trying to say behind the words.
Your friend says arguing about it is pointless: 'There is no ___ in it.' Which word means 'sense' or 'purpose'?
b1-adj-jaehrlich: Your gym fee is not paid every month. You pay one big amount in January, and then nothing until next January.
The company publishes a report every December, once in twelve months and never more often.
On a form you read that the fee is paid once every twelve months. Which word means 'yearly'?
b1-n-kerze: The power goes out at night. You light a small stick of wax with a flame so you can see in the living room.
On a birthday cake, you blow out the little sticks with tiny flames before you make a wish.
You want something with wax and a wick to put on the table for a romantic dinner. Which word means 'candle'?
b1-v-aufschreiben: Your teacher says a phone number only once. You quickly take a pen and put it on paper so you do not lose it.
At the doctor's you hear many instructions. You take notes so you remember them at home.
A friend tells you a recipe over the phone. Which verb means 'to write down'?
b1-adv-naemlich: You are late and explain: 'I could not come earlier. The bus ___ did not run.' Which little word gives the reason in a gentle, explaining way?
You say: 'I know two people who can help, ___ Anna and Tom.' Which word introduces the exact names, like 'namely'?
Your boss asks why you are so tired. You explain, adding a small word meaning 'you see, the reason is': 'The baby cried all night.'
b1-n-oeffentlichkeit: A famous singer never talks to journalists. She wants to keep her private life away from everybody who reads the news.
The police ask all the people of the town to help find a missing child. Whom do they ask? They ask 'the general ___'.
A company must tell everyone outside the firm about the problem with its product. Which word means 'the public'?
b1-n-picknick: On a sunny Sunday you spread a blanket on the grass in the park and eat sandwiches and fruit from a basket.
The family wants to eat outdoors next to the lake, with food they brought from home.
Your friend plans a meal outside on a meadow and asks you to bring drinks. Which word means 'picnic'?
b1-v-sich-eignen: You ask the shop assistant whether these thin summer shoes are good enough for walking in snow. He says they are not right for that.
A teacher asks if this difficult text is the right level for beginners. Is it appropriate for them?
You wonder if a wooden table can work as a desk. Which verb means 'to be suitable'?
b1-n-dach: Rain drips into your attic. You call a worker to repair the top covering of the house where the tiles are.
A cat sits on the highest part of the house, on the tiles above the attic.
A child draws a house: a square for the walls and a triangle on top. What is the triangle?
b1-adj-spitz: You draw with a new pencil that has a very thin tip. Its end is not round at all.
In geometry class, the teacher draws an angle smaller than 90 degrees. What kind of angle is it?
Be careful with the sewing needle! Its end is very narrow and can hurt your finger. Which word means 'pointed'?
b1-n-kraftfahrzeug: On an official form, a box asks for the registration of any road vehicle with an engine, like a car, truck or motorbike. What formal word is used?
A road sign says this street is closed to all vehicles driven by an engine, such as cars, trucks and motorbikes.
At the office you register your car for tax and insurance. The clerk uses a formal term for any engine-driven road vehicle. Which word means 'motor vehicle'?
b1-n-tod: Your neighbour's grandfather was very old. Last night his heart stopped and he was no longer alive. The family is sad.
A newspaper reports that a famous actor passed away at the age of 90.
A card in the post says: 'We are sad about the ___ of our friend.' Which word means 'death'?
b1-v-auftreten: A band will be on stage at the city festival tonight. They will play in front of the audience.
The doctor says that headaches can sometimes show up as a side effect of this medicine.
A problem suddenly comes up during your project. Which verb means 'to occur' or 'to arise'?
b1-n-mahnung: You forgot to pay your phone bill. A letter arrives asking you firmly to pay and says extra fees will follow.
Your library book is two weeks late. The library sends you a note asking you to return it.
The gym writes that you still owe money, and it is already the second written notice. Which word means 'reminder'?
b1-adj-wertvoll: Your grandmother gives you an old gold ring that is worth a lot of money and means a lot to the family.
A museum keeps a very old painting behind glass because it is worth millions.
A friend's advice helped you so much that you say it was very precious to you. Which adjective means 'valuable'?
b1-n-burg: On a school trip you climb a hill to see a medieval stone building with towers and thick walls where knights once lived.
In a fairy tale a king lives behind high walls on a hill, with guards at the gate.
A tourist guide shows you the old fortress above the river town. Which word means 'castle'?
b1-v-abwaschen: After dinner the plates, glasses and pots are dirty in the sink. Your mother asks you to clean them with soap and water.
You have no dishwasher. Every evening one person stands at the sink and cleans the dishes by hand.
There is mud all over your bike. You use a hose to get it off. Which verb means 'to wash off'?
b1-n-benzin: The warning light on your car's tank is on. You stop at a station to fill it with fuel, not diesel.
Your lawn mower will not start. Your neighbour says it needs the liquid fuel from the can in the garage.
The price of fuel for cars went up again. Which word means 'petrol'?
b1-n-fortsetzung: You loved the film last year. Now the cinema shows part two of the story with the same actors.
A magazine story ends with 'To be continued next week.' You wait for the next part.
The meeting stops at noon, and the rest will go on tomorrow morning. Which word means 'continuation'?
b1-n-operation: The doctor says your appendix must be removed. You will sleep under anesthesia while a surgeon cuts and fixes it.
Your grandfather's hip is being fixed in the hospital, and you wait for three hours with the family.
Your friend broke a bone badly and needs surgery. Which word means 'operation'?
b1-adv-damit: You hold a hammer in your hand. Your friend asks what you plan to do with it. Which small word means 'with it'?
Your friend gives you a fragile gift and says: 'Be careful ___!' Which word means 'with that'?
A technician points at a broken machine and asks if you know how to work with it. Which small word means 'with that'?
b1-v-veraendern: Your hairdresser cuts your long hair very short. You look completely different from before.
After moving to a new city, you notice your habits are not the same as before. The city made you different.
You open the design file and make small adjustments to the colors. Which verb means 'to alter'?
b1-adj-zahlreich: At the football match there were so many fans that the stadium was completely full, a huge number of people.
The bookshop has hundreds of cookbooks on its shelves, a great many.
The teacher says the students sent a large number of questions after the lesson. Which adjective means 'numerous'?
b1-n-pflicht: In many countries, every child must go to school. It is not a choice, because the law says you have to.
As a lifeguard, you have to watch the swimmers. It is part of your job, and you cannot skip it.
Voting is a right, but paying taxes is something you must do. Which word means 'duty'?
b1-n-rueckkehr: After two years abroad, your sister comes back home next week. The family prepares a welcome party for her arrival.
The astronauts' journey back from space to Earth was successful.
The travel plan says: 'Day 7: going back to the place where we started.' Which word means 'return'?
b1-v-entlassen: The company has no money left. The boss tells fifty workers that they must leave their jobs and will not be paid any more.
After a week in hospital, the doctor says you may go home today.
The boss is angry because Tom is late every day. He tells him to leave and not come back. Which verb means 'to fire'?
b1-n-blut: You cut your finger with a knife and a red liquid comes out. You press a tissue on it.
At the doctor's, a nurse puts a needle in your arm to take a sample for a test.
A campaign asks healthy people to donate the red liquid that flows in the veins to help patients. What is it called?
b1-n-suchtmittel: A health leaflet warns about alcohol, nicotine and drugs that people can become dependent on.
A doctor tells a patient to stay away from anything that can make a person addicted, like tobacco.
At school, a talk is about substances that can lead to dependence. Which word means 'addictive substance'?
b1-adj-elektrisch: A car has no petrol engine. It runs on a battery that you charge at a socket.
A sign on a fence says that power runs through the wire and touching it hurts.
Your toothbrush works with a battery and vibrates by itself. Which adjective means 'electric'?
b1-v-sich-befinden: A friend calls: 'Where are you right now?' You answer, in a formal way, that you are currently at the airport.
After the operation, the nurse politely asks how you feel. You answer that you feel fine.
The museum guide says the old paintings are located in the east wing. Which verb means 'to be located'?
b1-n-kakao: On a cold winter morning a child drinks something warm and sweet made of milk and chocolate powder.
The baker's recipe uses a brown powder that gives chocolate its taste.
At the café the kids order a warm chocolate drink with milk. Which word means 'hot chocolate' or 'cocoa'?
b1-n-einwohner: A small town has twelve thousand people living in it. A man who lives there is, for the town, one of these.
The mayor speaks to the people who live in the village, to every man who lives there.
The statistics office counts how many people live in Berlin. Which word means a male 'inhabitant'?
b1-n-wunde: You fall off your bike and the skin on your knee is open and red. You clean it and put a plaster on it.
The nurse changes the bandage on the cut where the surgeon worked.
A football player has an open cut above his eye after a hard knock. Which word means 'wound'?
b1-v-reagieren: You tell your friend some surprising news, and you watch how he answers with his face and words.
You email your landlord about the broken heater, but he never answers. You wonder why he does not respond.
A driver sees a child run into the street and brakes immediately. He had to act fast. Which verb means 'to react'?
b1-adj-begrenzt: The parking lot has only twenty places for hundreds of visitors, so space is not unlimited.
A sign says only ten people may enter the room at the same time. The number is restricted.
You have only fifty euros for the whole month, so your money can only go so far. Which adjective means 'limited'?
b1-n-geheimnis: Your friend tells you something personal and asks you not to tell anyone. You promise.
In a detective story nobody knows why the door was locked from the inside. Something remains unexplained.
At a surprise party the guests hide the plan from the birthday girl. Which word means 'secret'?
b1-n-senior: An old man of 70 pays a cheaper price at the museum because of his age.
A club for retired people offers chess and coffee afternoons. A man who is 72 joins it.
At the pharmacy, an advert offers a free health check for people over 65. Which word means a male 'senior citizen'?
b1-adv-bloss: A shop assistant asks if you need help. You answer politely that you are only looking, nothing more.
You say the repair cost just ten euros, nothing more. Which small word means 'only'?
Your friend ate a tiny piece of cake and says it was simply a taste. Which little word means 'just'?
b1-v-folgen: You walk behind your guide through the forest, staying close and going where she goes.
On your phone you see a friend's posts every day because you subscribed to her account.
The teacher speaks so fast that you cannot keep up with her explanation as it goes along. Which verb means 'to follow'?
b1-n-sack: At the farm, potatoes are packed in a big, rough bag that holds many kilos.
Father Christmas carries the toys on his back in a big cloth bag.
You buy cement. It is sold in a heavy paper bag of 25 kilos. Which word means 'sack'?
b1-n-empfehlung: You ask the waiter which dish is the best. He suggests the fish soup.
Your old boss writes a letter for your new job application saying you are a good worker.
A friend tells you about a great film you should see. She gives you a tip. Which word means 'recommendation'?
b1-adj-verdaechtig: A man stands next to a car at night and looks into every window. The neighbours think he may be up to no good.
A bag lies alone in the station and nobody knows whose it is. It looks strange.
You get an email from an unknown sender asking for your bank password. It looks like a trick. Which adjective means 'suspicious'?
b1-n-ueberschrift: On a newspaper page, big bold letters at the top tell you what the article is about.
When writing an essay, you put a short line in large letters above the first paragraph.
The teacher says each section of your homework needs a short name at the top. Which word means 'heading'?
b1-v-gebrauchen: Your neighbour wants to throw away a good chair. You say: 'Wait, I could put that to good use in my room.'
You read the instructions that explain how a drill is handled to make holes in the wall.
A friend gives you old clothes, and you say you can really find a purpose for them. Which verb means 'to use'?
b1-n-fremdsprache: At school you learn English, French or Spanish besides your mother tongue.
A job ad says that knowledge of at least one language other than your own is required.
In Bangladesh, students study Bengali as their own language and English as a second one from abroad. Which word means 'foreign language'?
b1-n-weiterbildung: You have worked as an accountant for ten years. Now you attend evening courses to learn new software and improve your skills for your job.
Your boss pays for a weekend seminar to help you grow in your profession.
A flyer offers courses for adults who already work and want to learn more. Which word means 'further training'?
b1-v-retten: A child falls into the river and a passer-by jumps in and pulls him out, so he does not drown.
Your laptop is dying, but you manage to keep your thesis from being lost just in time.
Firefighters carry people out of a burning house. Which verb means 'to rescue'?
b1-adj-kritisch: The film critic writes a review that points out many weaknesses of the new movie.
The doctor says the patient's condition is serious and could become dangerous in the next hours.
A student does not simply believe everything in the news and checks the facts carefully. Which adjective describes this attitude: 'critical'?
b1-n-reklame: Between your favourite TV show, short films try to make you buy a new shampoo.
Your mailbox is full of colourful papers offering cheap pizza and furniture.
A big poster at the bus stop shows a car and a slogan. Which word means 'advertising'?
b1-n-teilnahme: You sign up for the city marathon. The form says that taking part costs 20 euros.
The teacher writes that being present at the workshop is required for the certificate.
Your company asks if you will come to the Christmas party. Which word means 'participation'?
b1-v-ausrichten: Your colleague is out. The caller asks you to pass on a message to her when she returns.
You hang pictures on the wall and adjust them so that they are all in a straight line.
Your mother says: 'When you see Grandpa, please give him my greetings.' Which verb means 'to tell' someone a message?
b1-n-karotte: A rabbit chews a long, orange vegetable that grows underground.
You make soup and peel orange root vegetables with a peeler.
At the market you buy a kilo of long orange roots. Which word means 'carrot'?
b1-n-haut: After a day at the beach without sun cream, the outer covering of your body is red and hurts.
A doctor checks a strange spot on the outside of your body.
The label of a cream says that it keeps your body's outer covering soft. Which word means 'skin'?
b1-adv-schliesslich: You tried three restaurants and discussed many ideas. After a long talk you decided on pizza, as the last step.
A friend says: 'Do not be angry with him. He is your brother, after all.'
After waiting an hour at the station, the bus came at last. Which adverb means 'finally'?
b1-adj-musikalisch: Your daughter sings in tune and plays the piano by ear. She has a talent for music.
Your son always hums perfect tunes and keeps the rhythm, even though he never took lessons.
A friend of yours is gifted with sounds and rhythm. Which adjective means 'musical'?
b1-n-kauf: You paid 800 euros at the electronics store and left with a new laptop. The shop gave you a receipt.
A family signs papers to get a house, a big step after years of saving.
On the website you press the button to buy the items in your basket. Which word means 'purchase'?
b1-v-einschalten: It is dark in the room. You press a button on the wall so the lamp comes on.
You sit on the sofa, take the remote and press the red button so the picture appears.
Your laptop is off. You press the power button to start it. Which verb means 'to switch on'?
b1-n-einleitung: You open a book and read the first pages that explain what the book is about before the real chapters start.
In your essay, the first paragraph gives the topic and says what you will discuss.
At a presentation, the speaker begins with a few opening words. Which word means 'introduction'?
b1-n-serie: You watch an episode every evening of a story that has several seasons on a streaming service.
A car maker announces a new model line that will be produced in large numbers.
The football team won five games one after another. Which word means 'series'?
b1-v-einsetzen: You get a new battery and place it into the remote control.
At half time, the coach decides to bring the young striker onto the pitch and play him.
You take a missing puzzle piece and put it into the empty space. Which verb means 'to insert'?
b1-n-haupt: You look for the most important street in a small town, not any side street. Which short word part means 'main'?
On the menu, the biggest dish of the meal comes after the starter. The first part of its name means 'main'.
In a film, the person who plays the leading role is called the 'main' actor. Which short word part means 'main'?
b1-adj-faellig: Your rent must be paid on the first of the month. Today is the first, so the payment has to be made now.
Your car's technical inspection date has come, so you must go now.
The gym fee has reached its payment date today. Which adjective means 'due'?
b1-n-abenteuer: You and your friends travel through a jungle with a map, not knowing what will happen next. It is an exciting and risky trip.
A boy reads a book about pirates searching for treasure on a faraway island.
Your friend quit his office job to sail around the world because he wants an exciting experience. Which word means 'adventure'?
b1-n-laufwerk: You put a DVD into your old computer. Which part of the PC takes it and reads it?
Your computer shows C: and D: as separate places where files are stored.
A technician says the unit inside your computer that stores files is broken. Which word means 'drive'?
b1-v-stecken: You push the USB stick into the computer port.
You search for your keys everywhere. Then you find them: they were in your jacket pocket all the time.
You push a rose into a vase so that it stands upright. Which verb means 'to put' or 'to stick'?
b1-n-tuch: You spilled water on the table. You grab a soft piece of fabric to wipe it.
It is cold outside. You wrap a piece of fabric around your neck.
You spread a big piece of fabric over the furniture before painting. Which word means 'cloth'?
b1-adj-tolerant: Your neighbour has different religious views from yours, but you respect them and do not mind.
A teacher accepts that students dress and think differently and never judges them.
A friend lets others live in their own way without complaining. Which adjective means 'tolerant'?
b1-n-heimweh: You study abroad. At night you miss your parents, your town and your own bed so much that you feel sad.
A child at summer camp cries because he wants to go back to his family home.
After three months in a foreign country, you feel a strong longing for your home. Which word means 'homesickness'?
b1-v-herausfinden: A detective checks all the details until he discovers who took the money.
You do not know when the shop opens. You look it up on the internet to get the answer.
Your friend wants to discover the truth about a rumour. Which verb means 'to find out'?
b1-n-profi: The plumber fixed your leak in ten minutes. You say: 'He really knows his job. He is a real ___.' Which word means 'pro'?
Your colleague solves computer problems quickly and without mistakes. She is certainly no beginner.
For your wedding photos you hire someone who does this as a job, not an amateur. Which word means 'professional'?
b1-adv-nachher: Right now you are busy. You tell your friend you will call him later, when your work is over.
First we eat dinner, and after that we will watch a film.
You say: 'Let's talk about it ___.' Which adverb means 'afterwards'?
b1-n-gesamt: You add up all the costs of the trip: hotel, flights and food. The result is the full sum. Which short word part means 'total'?
A school reports the overall number of students in all classes together. Which short word part means 'total'?
The teacher gives a final grade made out of all your exam parts together. Which short word part means 'overall'?
b1-v-beschaeftigen: A large supermarket gives work and pays wages to two hundred people.
A mother gives the kids a puzzle to keep them busy while she cooks.
The article says the company has 500 people on its payroll. Which verb means 'to employ'?
b1-n-bau: Every morning loud machines and cranes work where a new house is being made, with workers in helmets.
Your uncle works as a bricklayer, putting up houses.
In the city there is a huge new structure with cranes around it, still unfinished. Which word means 'construction'?
b1-adj-gemuetlich: It is raining outside, and you sit on a soft sofa with a blanket, tea and candles. Everything feels warm and relaxed.
A small café has wooden tables, soft light and armchairs, and guests like to stay for hours.
Your friend says her new flat is small but feels warm and homely. Which adjective means 'cosy'?
b1-n-profisportler: A footballer gets a salary from a big club and trains every day. Sport is how he earns his living.
A tennis player travels around the world and wins prize money.
Your cousin does not play just for fun at the weekend, he earns a living from sport. Which word means a male 'professional athlete'?
b1-n-kabel: Your phone charger has a long thin line covered in plastic that goes from the plug to the phone.
Your TV picture is gone. Someone pulled the cord behind the cabinet.
Electricians run copper lines through the walls of a new building. Which word means 'cable'?
b1-v-protestieren: People gather on the street with signs, shouting that they do not agree with the price increase.
A student openly says to the teacher that the grade is unfair.
Neighbours stand peacefully in front of the town hall to show they are against a new road. Which verb means 'to protest'?
b1-n-luft: In the morning you open the window to let in fresh something we breathe.
A bicycle tyre is flat. You use a pump to fill it with the invisible gas around us.
In the mountains it is hard to breathe because there is less of it. Which word means 'air'?
b1-n-schwierigkeit: You try to open an online account, but the website keeps failing. It is a problem that makes it hard for you.
Learning a new language has many hard parts, like pronouncing strange sounds.
The teacher asks which part of the lesson was the hardest. Which word means 'difficulty'?
b1-adj-begeistert: Your team just won the final. You jump, shout and cannot stop smiling because you are full of joy.
A child unwraps a present and finds a puppy. She is delighted.
After the concert, the fans clap and talk, full of energy. Which adjective means 'enthusiastic'?
b1-v-begegnen: You walk through the park and by chance see your old teacher coming the other way.
On your trip you come across a strange animal on the road.
When travelling, you often meet people with different customs by chance. Which verb means 'to encounter'?
b1-n-geschwindigkeit: A road sign shows 50. The police use a camera to check how fast cars go.
A sprinter's result is measured by how fast he moves over 100 metres.
Your internet provider promises a fast connection. Which word means 'speed'?
b1-n-verhaeltnis: You and your boss get along well and trust each other. How would you describe the connection between you two?
A recipe says to mix flour and sugar two to one.
A report compares the number of men to the number of women in the team. Which word means 'ratio' or 'proportion'?
b1-n-faehigkeit: A job ad asks what you can do well, like languages, programming and driving. You list these.
After the accident, the patient lost the power to walk.
A child can remember faces after seeing them only once. Which word means 'ability'?
b1-v-entsorgen: Your old fridge does not work any more. You take it to a special place to have it properly got rid of.
Used batteries must not go in the normal rubbish, so you bring them to a collection box.
After a repair, the workers get rid of the old paint cans. Which verb means 'to dispose of'?
b1-adv-extra: The hotel price does not include breakfast. You must pay for it as an addition.
You baked this cake specially for your friend's birthday, not for anyone else.
You ask for the sauce in a small bowl on the side, kept apart from the pasta. Which word means 'separately' or 'extra'?
b1-adj-schlank: A model has a thin, graceful body and no extra weight.
Your friend started jogging and now fits into smaller jeans. She looks light and slim.
A shop assistant says this cut of trousers is made for people with a narrow body. Which adjective means 'slim'?
b1-n-fahrzeug: A police officer asks for the documents of your car, bus or truck, the general word for anything that carries people on a road.
A sign says the parking lot is only for cars, vans and motorcycles, anything that drives on wheels.
A bus, a bike, a truck, a car: what is the general word that covers all of them? Which word means 'vehicle'?
b1-n-fett: After frying bacon, a yellowish oily substance stays in the pan.
A nutrition label shows how many grams of this nutrient the chips contain. Too much is unhealthy.
A mechanic puts a thick, oily substance on the bike chain. Which word means 'grease'?
b1-v-bieten: At an auction you raise your hand and say you will pay 500 euros for the painting.
A hotel says its rooms give guests a view of the sea, a pool and free breakfast.
The company wants to give you a new job with better pay. Which verb means 'to offer'?
b1-n-schatten: On a hot day you move under a tree where the sun does not reach, and it feels cooler.
In the evening your dark outline stretches long across the road behind you as the sun goes down.
A child makes funny animal shapes on the wall with her hands in front of a lamp. Which word means 'shadow'?
b1-n-grund: Your friend did not come to the party. You ask why, because you want to hear the cause.
A swimmer dives down and touches the lowest part of the lake.
The teacher says: 'You have no ___ to be nervous.' Which word means 'reason'?
b1-adj-vergeblich: You tried for an hour to open the stuck door, but nothing worked and you gave up.
He waited at the station all night, but she never came. His effort brought no result.
All the searching for the lost key was pointless. Which adjective means 'futile'?
b1-v-ansprechen: At the party you see an interesting person and decide to go over and start talking to her.
You want to bring up a problem with your boss at the meeting.
A stranger in the street walks up and speaks to you to ask for directions. Which verb means 'to address' someone?
b1-n-erholung: After a hard year at work, you spend two weeks at the beach, doing nothing and relaxing.
After the flu, the doctor says you need time to get better and regain strength.
A sign at the spa says it is a place for rest and relaxation. Which word means 'recovery'?
b1-n-sportart: The school asks: which kind of sport do you like, football, swimming, tennis or basketball?
At the Olympics there are many different disciplines such as running, boxing and rowing.
A form for the club asks you to tick which sport you want to do. Which word means 'type of sport'?
b1-n-konkurrenz: Two bakeries on the same street try to win the same customers. Each watches what the other does.
A company worries because rivals sell a similar phone for less money.
In a race, many other runners are trying to win against you. Which word means 'competition'?
b1-v-installieren: You download a new program and run the setup so it works on your laptop.
A technician fits a new washing machine in your kitchen and connects it to the water.
Your phone asks if you want to put a new app on it. Which verb means 'to install'?
b1-n-trainer: A man stands at the side of the football pitch, shouting instructions to the team and choosing the players.
At the gym a man shows you how to lift weights correctly and writes your plan.
A children's swimming club has a man who teaches the kids. Which word means a male 'coach'?
